common_name: Summer Wave Amethyst Torenia (Trailing Heat-Tolerant Shade Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March-May and again August-September. Summer Wave Amethyst is a trailing variety that cascades in hanging baskets, window boxes, and over the edges of raised beds, blooming continuously without deadheading in shade.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil. Summer Wave Amethyst bears snapdragon-like flowers in a rich purple-amethyst shade with a small yellow throat mark, part of the Suntory Flowers Summer Wave series bred for superior heat tolerance and continuous flowering without deadheading in shaded conditions where standard impatiens may struggle in humid summer heat. The trailing habit, spreading 24-36 inches on stems only 6-10 inches tall, makes it exceptional for hanging baskets, window boxes, and shade containers where the cascading stems display flowers at eye level. Torenia thrives in the moist, warm, shaded conditions typical of a Gulf South summer, and the wishbone-shaped stamens inside each flower give the plant its common name.
sources: Suntory Flowers — Summer Wave Torenia Introduction
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Annual Flowers for Shaded Areas

common_name: Catalina Midnight Blue Torenia (Heat-Tolerant Trailing Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March-May and again August-September. Part of the Catalina series of heat-tolerant trailing torenia bred by PanAmerican Seed.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil. Catalina Midnight Blue bears snapdragon-like flowers in an intensely deep, almost navy blue-purple, part of the Catalina series bred for improved heat tolerance and a semi-trailing habit well suited to hanging baskets and window boxes as well as shaded garden beds. It blooms continuously through the hottest part of summer without deadheading, providing color in shaded spots where few other annuals perform as reliably. Consistent moisture and a mostly shaded position keep the display at its best through Gulf South heat, and the wishbone-shaped stamens inside each flower give the plant its common name.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Annual Flowers for Shaded Areas

common_name: Duchess Royal Indigo Torenia (Compact Bicolor Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March-May and again August-September. Duchess is a compact, mounding torenia series bred for uniform bedding and container performance.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil. Duchess Royal Indigo bears snapdragon-like flowers with deep indigo-blue upper petals and a paler blue lower lip marked with a bright yellow throat, held on a compact, mounding plant bred for uniform bedding display rather than the trailing habit of the Summer Wave and Catalina series. Its tidy, dense growth suits mass plantings, edging, and small containers where a spreading trailing torenia would sprawl too much. It blooms continuously through summer heat without deadheading, and the wishbone-shaped stamens inside each flower give the plant its common name.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Annual Flowers for Shaded Areas
Louisiana State University AgCenter — Shade-Tolerant Annuals for Gulf South

common_name: Blue Troll Browallia (Classic Dwarf Compact Bush Violet)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape. A long-established, extra-dwarf classic Browallia cultivar popular for edging and hanging baskets.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape. Blue Troll is a long-established, extra-dwarf bush violet bred for a low, dense mound only a few inches tall, smothered in upward-facing, deep violet-blue, bell-shaped flowers with a small white eye. Its especially compact scale suits edging a shaded path, filling a small container, or the front of a mixed shade bed where taller Browallia cultivars would be out of proportion. Plants bloom continuously without deadheading.

common_name: White Troll Browallia (Classic Dwarf Compact White Bush Violet)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape. A long-established, extra-dwarf classic Browallia cultivar and white-flowered sibling of Blue Troll.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape. White Troll is a long-established, extra-dwarf bush violet bred for a low, dense mound only a few inches tall, smothered in upward-facing, pure white, bell-shaped flowers, the white-flowered sibling of Blue Troll. Its especially compact scale suits edging a shaded path, filling a small container, or the front of a mixed shade bed where taller Browallia cultivars would be out of proportion, and its pale color brightens dim corners effectively. Plants bloom continuously without deadheading.

common_name: Sunsatia Lemon Nemesia (Fragrant Trailing Yellow Nemesia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after hardening off into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Sunsatia nemesia flowers best in cool weather and can stall or decline during peak summer heat, part of a fragrant Proven Winners series.

directions: Plant transplants into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade. Sunsatia Lemon bears masses of small, sweetly fragrant, soft lemon-yellow flowers on a trailing, well-branched plant, part of the Proven Winners Sunsatia series bred for a pronounced, pleasant fragrance and improved heat tolerance compared with older nemesia strains. It performs best in the cooler months of a Gulf South growing season, blooming heavily in spring and fall and often slowing or pausing during the most intense summer heat before resuming as temperatures cool. Deadhead and shear lightly to encourage continued bloom, provide consistent moisture, and treat as a cool-season annual or short-lived perennial depending on climate.
